Back again with a doc on Akane’s strategy during Zero Time Dilemma. I’ll try to keep it short as like all my docs on Akane, this is mainly meant for people who have already played the ZE games and already understand the context these feats are performed under, so y’all are missing out on how impressive these feats really are if you haven’t played the games yourselves (which I recommend for anyone even outside of SCD).
Background:

Prior to the Decision Games, Akane and Delta had reached a compromise and made an uneasy alliance in order to take down the religious terrorist that threatened all of humanity. Delta already knew who this terrorist was but refused to tell Akane because then she wouldn’t need Delta anymore and wouldn’t need to use Radical-6. On top of that, the Radical-6 apocalypse is what led to Delta’s birth to begin with, so Akane was forced into incorporating the apocalypse into her grand plan. 6 billion lives is worth it to avoid total human extinction.

This is the background to Akane’s grand plan which I have dubbed her “Perfect Future” plan. Her goal was simple: Create a timeline where Radical-6 never happened and allow for her and Junpei to spend the rest of their lives together in peace. Since Junpei would forever hate her if he learnt that Akane is partly responsible for Radical-6, she had decided to build her Decision Game plan around framing Delta for it all and Delta gladly accepted the role, likely because Akane was the one who held the keys to Delta’s whole life.

The Decision Games itself can be scaled to both Akane and Delta as it was a team effort and the extent to which either one planned the games over the other is unknown, but it makes the most sense to scale it fully to Akane because she was the one with knowledge on other timelines meanwhile Delta couldn’t access any of them without mind hacking her first.
With that out of the way, we can examine what Akane’s strategy for the Decision Games was and how she made her Perfect Future possible.
Part 1: The Decision Games

In the Mars Mission Test site, 9 players are imprisoned by Delta and are forced into choosing the result of a coinflip. This splits the timeline in two, the timeline where they won the coinflip and are free to go, and the timeline where they lose the coinflip and are forced into playing the Decision Games, where most of Zero Time Dilemma takes place. After they lose the coin flip, the players are split into 3 groups of 3.
C Team: Akane,  Junpei,  Carlos
Q Team: Mira, Sean, Eric
D Team: Sigma, Diana,  Phi

Akane integrates herself into C-Team for two reasons. One, because she would take any reason to be close to Junpei and two, because it creates the dual function of setting up the Transporter Strategy (will get into later) and allows her to more believably frame Delta for being the mastermind behind the games. Delta went around calling himself Zero II and proudly proclaims that he’s the one behind it all at the end, so why would Junpei suspect Akane at all?

The Decision Games basic premise goes as follows: All players have an X-Pass ascribed to them that’s only activated upon their death. In order to escape, they need to collect at least 6 X-Passes, meaning that 6/9 players must die in order for the remaining 3 to leave the games (notably, the 3 players don’t have to be on the same team).

On top of this, all 9 players are given a watch that contains a drug called Soporil which triggers memory loss. These watches are used to erase the memories of the round they just played, which leads to ZTD’s non-linear setting where the player is free to pick and choose exactly where and when in the game they are playing. From the players POV, every round they play is their first, with them only being able to tell how much time passed based on the time on their watches (unless they killed players, in this case Delta makes them keep their memories of that). This allowed for the use of SHIFTing between the “fragments” of the games, which was Akane’s intent all along and you’ll see why shortly.

At the beginning of the games, all teams are given an option to vote to execute one of the other teams. Once a team is given two votes, that team is executed. In order to prevent this, Carlos uses Gabs the dog in order to send messages to the other teams by stuffing it into his collar so they can spread the votes evenly. From here on out, I will be focusing the events in terms of what the Teams go through instead of what happens in each timeline all at once. The important thing to keep in mind is that some events in, for example, Timeline 0 can only be triggered by events that happen in Timeline 1. This format of things in timelines being locked behind a key that can only be found in other timelines is the key to the entire Force Quit strategy, it’s the reason why X-Passes are different depending on what timeline the players are in (each player has 3 different X-Pass passwords)which stops players from accessing memories from timelines where they killed 6 players and just leaving like that. It is also the key behind the Force Quit box itself, which I’ll get into explaining now.
Part 2: The Force Quit Box

The Force Quit box is a box found in the lounge by every team within the Decision Game. Its conditions for activating are different depending on which team is faced with it, but the basic premise is that teams have no way of using this box or even knowing what it’s for unless they jump through the exact timelines that Akane and Delta need them to jump through. For C Team, the passcode is “VIVEHODIE”, latin for “live for today”. For Q Team, the password is “38080832”, which Sean gets from the Quantum Computer and lastly for D Team, they need to insert two key items in order to activate it, that being the blue bird necklace that Diana has and Phi’s brooch.

Despite not being told its purpose, the name being “Force Quit” and the fact that the teams had to regain their memories of the alternate timelines they SHIFTed through made every team assume that it’s the device used to quit the Decision Game. This assumption was wrong, it’s actually the self-destruct code for the entire facility. I’ll explore why this happens in the end. For now, we can finally examine the ways each team came to unlock their respective Force Quit passcodes.

If you chose not to inject, Mira takes a vial of Radical-6 anyways, this comes back up later in D-END 1 as the exact vial Mira uses on Phi, making her Patient 0 of the entire outbreak. If you choose to inject, Mira goes on to kill Sean and Eric in a Radical frenzy since the FBR virus was a lie. We’ll come back to this timeline later

In Timeline 2, Sean and Eric wake up in the Pod Room with Mira missing. After this room, they discover Mira’s dead body in a pod and Eric points a shotgun to Sean asking who killed her. If Sean answers that Eric killed her, Eric just slimes him out

If Sean says he doesn’t know, Eric eventually puts down the gun and tells his pathetic chud backstory. Following this, Eric and Sean get a note from Carlos in C Team sent via Gabs the dog, telling them to check the family portrait in the Pod Room. They find the hint “twins birthday” on a yellow door, they begin re-investigating Mira before being knocked out by Delta and the memory loss drug in their watches (the hint feeds into D-Team, player POV fuckery)

Back in Timeline 1, after the inject timeline. Sean wakes back up and sees that Mira has killed other people and escaped through the X Door. Sean questions why he’s even alive if he had been “killed” by Mira, to which Delta comes back on TV and tells Sean to meet him at the Quantum Computer

Delta explains that Sean is a robot whose memories are tied to the Quantum Computer, giving him the illusion of being a human that can SHIFT. Delta gives Sean his helmet code which will come back up later

Back in Timeline 2 again, after the yellow door stuff and after Eric kills Carlos in front of everyone (long story), Eric threatens to kill Sean again, to which Sean offers to take off his helmet to explain everything, having gotten his memories from Timeline 1. Sean explains to everyone that he’s a robot and also points out Zero’s real name: Delta. Delta gets up from his wheelchair and explains to the players remaining what’s up.

Together, they all head to the Quantum Computer which Sean tries to access, but needs a code in order to do so. Eric holds Delta at gunpoint to give up the code which Delta nonchalantly agrees to, the code is 3808-0832, the exact code needed for Q Team Force Quit Box. After giving up that code, Delta had no more use for this timeline and mind hacks Eric to slime everyone except his mama Diana out.

Now in Timeline 4, where all teams survive after two rounds of Delta inducing the teams to vote against each other. Q Team is confronted with the Force Quit Box which tells them to turn on the central Quantum Computer in order to activate the Force Quit box. Using his memories from the other timelines, Sean is able to boot the computer and activate their team’s condition for the Force Quit box

If Diana does shoot and it’s a blank and everyone lives, they meet back up in the lounge and it’s discovered that all of D Team has been poisoned thanks to shenanigans from C-Team earlier. In Timeline 3, following the branch where Phi is fried in the incinerator. Sigma and Diana wake back up and have no idea what happened to Phi thanks to memory loss. They come across the Transporter Room and Delta explains that the Transporter can copy and replicate a maximum of 2 bodies at one time and send it back through its own history, spitting out an exact clone at a certain point in time. After solving the escape room, Sigma and Diana learn that everyone except them and Akane are dead, and that Akane has left through the X Door, trapping the two of them in the facility permanently.

With no other options, they elect to use the Transporter to send clones of themselves into another history. The original Sigma and Diana, however, remain trapped inside the facility, as the Transporter only sends cloned atomic data and not the actual person. Now with truly nothing left to do but wait for an Akane that will never return, Sigma and Diana eventually bond with each other. This results in them eventually having fraternal twins, a boy and a girl. They name the boy Delta and the girl Phi, these are the very same Delta and Phi that we know from the games. This is D END 2 and this whole thing was planned to ensure Delta’s birth (Phi’s as well but she’s an afterthought)

Meanwhile, the cloned Sigma and Diana get transported to Timeline 2, where the original versions of themselves from that timeline were executed. This eventually leads into the stuff already discussed in the Q Team section where eventually Delta slimes em all except for Diana (mama's boy) after giving Sean the Force Quit code so I won’t bother with this timeline. Part 4: Conclusion
(Keikaku Doori…)
Finally, we reach the ultimate end result of the activation of all team’s Force Quit boxes.

After each team activates their box and Q and C Team prevents their injection, all the teams meet up with each other in the lounge. Everyone except Mira and Eric, who are not Espers, reveal that they remember everything that happened in all the other histories. The players all reveal what they did to get to this point in regards to their boxes. As they ponder how they became aware of the other histories, Delta reveals himself. He explains that neither C or D team followed a linear flow of time in order to reach this point. Delta yaps some more, revealing his and Phi’s backstory and stopping Phi from activating the Force Quit box by placing the brooch in it. Phi, in a rage at Delta’s BS, dropkicks him to the floor, knocking Delta’s shotgun out of his arms to which Eric picks it up and points it at him. Thinking that they have the upper hand, they finally activate the Force Quit box for real this time (D Team didn’t actually insert their items at first, sorry if that part was confusing).

Just as they do, the facility alarm sounds off saying that the facility will explode in 10 minutes. This is the final twist, the Force Quit box wasn’t to exit the Decision Game, it was to blow up the whole facility. Delta, using his mind hacking ability, makes Eric shoot him in the chest, killing him nearly instantly (not dying without taunting em first, of course). Now with no advantages at all, the players question what they’re supposed to do next. It is right then that Akane comes up with a solution, they all SHIFT to the timeline where they won the coinflip, all the way back at the very beginning of the Game (which forces the versions that won on their first try to die in an explosion, a very interesting moral dilemma).

Together, with their powers combined, all 9 players SHIFT out of their bodies and into the version of themselves that won the coin flip, before the Decision Game event began (yes, Mira and Eric were able to SHIFT somehow). After this, Delta approaches the group and yaps about the purpose of the Game, I’ll spare you the details.
Final Result of this Strategy:

Akane and Delta work together to both cause and prevent the Radical-6 apocalypse. They needed it to happen in order to take down the Religious Fanatic together, something neither could accomplish alone. The Radical-6 apocalypse is what led to Delta’s birth to begin with so after they did that, they created another timeline where it never happened yet Delta is born anyways. This is the CQD END 2 timeline at the end of the game, what this Force Quit strategy led to, a timeline where nobody dies and Akane is free to spend the rest of her life with Junpei in peace after dealing with the threat of the Fanatic.
